event.title: Moscow Restaurant Bombing
event.summary: An explosion occurred at a restaurant in central Moscow, killing three people and injuring at least 15 others. Security officials reported that a woman attempted to enter the restaurant with explosives but was stopped by a security guard before the device detonated. Investigators and emergency services are currently at the scene.

timeline.title: Bombing at Moscow Restaurant Kills Three and Injures Many
timeline.summary: A bombing at an upscale Italian restaurant in central Moscow resulted in the deaths of three people and injuries to at least 21 others. The explosion occurred on Saturday evening, reportedly caused by a homemade bomb carried by a woman. Russian authorities have suggested that the attack may be linked to the ongoing conflict with Ukraine, with some speculation that a senior military figure was the intended target.

event_overview.title: About Terrorism
event_overview.subject: Terrorism
event_overview.summary: The event is a bombing at Balzi Rossi, an Italian restaurant in central Moscow, on August 1, 2026. Early official and media accounts reported three deaths, including the alleged bomber, and more than 20 injuries; later reporting indicated that the casualty count was being revised as authorities assessed the attack and its aftermath.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The blast occurred on the evening of August 1, 2026, at the Balzi Rossi restaurant in central Moscow.

facts.label: Initial casualties
facts.value: Russian officials initially reported at least three deaths, including the woman described in reporting as the bomber, and at least 21 people wounded.

facts.label: Method reported
facts.value: Reporting cited Russian accounts that an explosive device was detonated at the restaurant; one account said a suspicious package carried by a woman posing as a delivery worker was remotely activated.

facts.label: Official characterization
facts.value: Moscow's mayor described the incident as a terrorist act. Russian authorities and officials subsequently made allegations about responsibility, but those claims had not been independently established in the reporting consulted.

facts.label: Casualty-count uncertainty
facts.value: By August 3, reporting said the death toll had risen to five and noted that the National Anti-Terrorism Committee had initially issued a lower figure, underscoring that casualty reporting was still evolving.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the initial August 1-3 reporting on the blast and changing casualty accounts, not any later investigation, prosecution, attribution finding, or broader history of attacks in Moscow.
